It should connect ARR scale to repeatability in product, go-to-market, or efficiency.
It should highlight that lessons from large SaaS companies are useful only when translated into founder actions.
rubric_must_haves: Uses a numbered or clearly segmented structure for the learnings.
Includes at least one financial or go-to-market implication.
Keeps the focus on what founders should do, not just what Monday.com achieved.
Avoids empty praise and turns observations into lessons.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer distills Monday.com's ARR milestone into a handful of practical founder lessons, such as the importance of product-led distribution, repeatable expansion, disciplined execution, or category focus. The best version does not simply admire the company; it explains what an earlier-stage founder should copy, what they should ignore, and why the operating lesson matters.

trace.answer:
So we’ve done so many SaaStr deep dives on Monday before, I didn’t think there was much more to learn.  But they keep scaling!
At $500m ARR Monday just keeps accelerating:
$500M ARR
Growing 100%
110% NRR
Free Cash Flow Margins of almost 30%, and even non-GAAP profits (profitable)
It’s truly an incredible engine at scale.
What can you learn here?  A few things:

#1.  Still Going Long — And Growing Even Faster Now
Monday still doesn’t really care if your deal size is big ($300k+) … or small ($20).  It’s all good for them.  The same percentage of their revenue comes from Small customers (<10 seats) as Big ones (>50), and that hasn’t changed since $120m in ARR when we first looked at this data below.
This isn’t unusual these days.  We also saw Asana do the exact same thing.  Go long, get creative, and find a way to serve everyone.
#2.  87% of Revenue From Outside North America
We’re seeing a lot of B2B leaders now grow outside of NA significantly, especially Cloudflare and ZoomInfo.  There aren’t any secrets here — go global!  You don’t need to understand another language or culture to sell to folks who speak English.
#3.  35% of Customers Pay Monthly, Up From 23% At $360m ARR
Again, going long is key.  Monday does offer annual discounts, but it doesn’t force them.  Instead, they let the deals run longer and encourage monthly payments.  More on that
here
.

retrieval_hits.text:
We
last looked in on Monday.com at $240m ARR
, but it’s grown so incredibly quickly, and so effectively, it’s worth checking in again at $400,000,000 in ARR.
Because at $400,000,000 in ARR …  Monday is growing a stunning 91% (!) year-over-year.  Goodness gracious!
5 Interesting Learnings:

#1.  Revenue up 91%, Customer Count Up “Just” 34%.  The math of going upmarket
.  I personally get a little worried when this ratio falls below 2:1, if only because sometimes upsell can mask lower growth in new accounts.  The real story with Monday is going upmarket.  $50k+ customers are up 200%, to 793 from 264 a year ago.  That’s a key driver to Monday’s hyper-growth as it approaches $500,000,000 in ARR.
#2.  10+ Users the Sweet Spot now
.  As part of going upmarket, Monday’s 10+ seat customers are now 72% of total revenue, up from 63% just a year ago.  Asana has seen similar dynamics, but Monday seems to be going upmarket even faster than Asana.

#7.  Monday.com is growing 68% (!) at $550m in ARR.  No SMB deceleration here!
Not much, at least.  Monday’s growth has slowed a little bit, but in absolute terms, the growth is just incredible even now.

.
@mondaydotcom
 crosses:

$1,000,000,000 in ARR
+34% Revenue Growth
110% NRR
22% Free Cash Flow Margins

Call it many things. But don't call it a downturn.

Go find your Monday.

So Monday.com has
filed to IPO
with some pretty incredible numbers, especially considering just how competitive the space is.
At $240m in ARR, they are growing a stunning 85% year-over-year!  And that’s with direct and indirect competition from Asana, Atlassian, Clickup, Wrike, Smartsheet, Notion and so many others.
Pretty incredible for a product that just launched in 2014.
Whoa.
5 Interesting Learnings:
#1.  121% NRR from 10+ seat customers, 107% overall, ~85% from smallest customers.
This is a super-helpful breakdown for anyone selling to customers both smaller and larger.  65% of its revenue comes from 10+ seat deals and they have 121% NRR.  The remaining 35% is from smaller deals.  For those to average to 107%, NRR is likely around 85% for self-service and < 10 seat deals (about the same as
Squarespace
).
So those seem like good yardsticks to shoot for if you sell to SMBs of all shapes and sizes and are somewhat like Monday.  The tiniest of customers may have only 85% NRR.  But once you cross 10 seats, you should start to see the benefits of account growth and 120% NRR like Monday.

Topic: 5 Interesting Learnings from Monday.com at $550,000,000 in ARR

[train_10049]
We
last looked in on Monday.com at $240m ARR
, but it’s grown so incredibly quickly, and so effectively, it’s worth checking in again at $400,000,000 in ARR.
Because at $400,000,000 in ARR …  Monday is growing a stunning 91% (!) year-over-year.  Goodness gracious!
5 Interesting Learnings:

#1.  Revenue up 91%, Customer Count Up “Just” 34%.  The math of going upmarket
.  I personally get a little worried when this ratio falls below 2:1, if only because sometimes upsell can mask lower growth in new accounts.  The real story with Monday is going upmarket.  $50k+ customers are up 200%, to 793 from 264 a year ago.  That’s a key driver to Monday’s hyper-growth as it approaches $500,000,000 in ARR.
#2.  10+ Users the Sweet Spot now
.  As part of going upmarket, Monday’s 10+ seat customers are now 72% of total revenue, up from 63% just a year ago.  Asana has seen similar dynamics, but Monday seems to be going upmarket even faster than Asana.

So Monday.com has
filed to IPO
with some pretty incredible numbers, especially considering just how competitive the space is.
At $240m in ARR, they are growing a stunning 85% year-over-year!  And that’s with direct and indirect competition from Asana, Atlassian, Clickup, Wrike, Smartsheet, Notion and so many others.
Pretty incredible for a product that just launched in 2014.
Whoa.
5 Interesting Learnings:
#1.  121% NRR from 10+ seat customers, 107% overall, ~85% from smallest customers.
This is a super-helpful breakdown for anyone selling to customers both smaller and larger.  65% of its revenue comes from 10+ seat deals and they have 121% NRR.  The remaining 35% is from smaller deals.  For those to average to 107%, NRR is likely around 85% for self-service and < 10 seat deals (about the same as
Squarespace
).
So those seem like good yardsticks to shoot for if you sell to SMBs of all shapes and sizes and are somewhat like Monday.  The tiniest of customers may have only 85% NRR.  But once you cross 10 seats, you should start to see the benefits of account growth and 120% NRR like Monday.<|eot_id|><|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>
